results.title: Development and Preliminary Validation of a Screener for Digital Health Readiness - PMC
results.content: ### Findings This qualitative study of a screener for digital health readiness, which measures technical readiness and quality-of-care concerns, included data from 367 participants. Patients and health care professionals were interviewed to explore barriers to telehealth use, scale items were developed for the screener, cognitive interviews were conducted to refine scale items, and psychometric properties of the screener were evaluated. This qualitative study develops and performs preliminary validity analysis of a tool to measure patients’ digital health readiness. These barriers include factors such as trust, acceptance, and understanding the relevance of telehealth as a means of receiving care, and they have been reported to independently be associated with lower uptake of telehealth.4,5,6,7,8 Expanding on the concept of digital readiness,4 our team adopted the term _digital health readiness_ to represent the overarching concept of people’s ability and comfort in using digital tools for health care engagement, inclusive of the many factors that extend beyond digital health literacy. We applied a conventional content analysis approach to identify themes related to digital health readiness with the purpose of extracting relevant data for use in item development of the tool. Converging evidence from the correlations with health literacy and the known-groups differences in technical readiness and quality-of-care concerns among the educational level attainment groups suggests that this tool is capturing what it was intended to capture, namely, how ready a patient might be for using various digital health services. Specifically, inclusion of quality-of-care concerns differentiates the tool from the recent Digital Health Readiness Questionnaire that was published by a team in Belgium, which included domains of digital use, digital skills, digital literacy, digital health literacy, and digital learnability.10 The screening tool in its entirety exemplifies the complexity of factors influencing digital health uptake among various populations and highlights several areas for potential intervention to support increased digital health uptake at both the individual and population levels. Future work is needed to design interventions to support patients identified as having specific digital health readiness barriers and inform development of a shorter version of the tool for routine implementation across clinical care sites.

Moreover, the integration of big data analytics and Bayesian statistics into psychometric validation is reshaping how researchers approach instrument development and evaluation. As these innovative statistical methods gain traction, they hold the potential to revolutionize psychometrics, paving the way for more effective and inclusive psychological assessment practices in an increasingly complex world.

results.title: Top Trends in Curriculum Development for 2024 - Sara Learning
results.content: In 2024, educators, institutions, and policymakers are embracing new approaches that focus on enhancing student engagement, promoting lifelong learning, and integrating technology. A well-structured curriculum serves as the foundation for effective teaching and learning, and keeping up with the latest trends in curriculum development is essential to ensure that students receive a well-rounded and relevant education. One of the most significant trends in curriculum development is the shift toward personalized learning. Rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, educators are designing curricula that can be tailored to individual student needs, learning styles, and interests. Personalized learning allows students to move at their own pace, choose areas of interest, and receive targeted support where needed. Adaptive learning platforms and data analytics provide insights into student performance, allowing educators to adjust the curriculum to suit each learner. This trend empowers students to take ownership of their education, making learning more engaging and effective. As digital tools become increasingly prevalent in everyday life, students need to develop digital literacy skills to thrive in the modern world. By embedding these elements into the curriculum, educators ensure that students are prepared for the digital challenges they will face in their personal and professional lives. Competency-based education (CBE) is gaining traction as a transformative approach to curriculum development. In recent years, there has been an increasing emphasis on the importance of social-emotional learning (SEL) in curriculum development. In 2024, educators are developing curricula that emphasize interconnectedness and the role students play in shaping a better world. Breaking down the traditional barriers between subjects, interdisciplinary learning is becoming a key focus in curriculum development. Interdisciplinary learning not only broadens students’ knowledge but also enhances critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. In 2024, curricula are increasingly designed to integrate various disciplines, allowing students to explore topics from multiple angles and apply their learning in innovative ways. These flexible approaches allow students to access education in ways that suit their circumstances, whether through in-person, remote, or blended learning environments. This trend not only increases accessibility but also provides opportunities for lifelong learning, as individuals can continue their education beyond the traditional classroom setting.
